\begin{CRchronicle}{107}
For three days after the Hearth Drawing the house under the Vail roof went about its tending as a surgeon goes about a field taken as found and left as found, and nothing seen two doors down crossed under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment. The yard went around its seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest around the returning line where a hand had gone in on Seed 15 and had not come out. Sella Vail came to the coals before she came to the basket, told them it was the thaw, turned them with the back of a broken pot, and said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would have said I. She lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first, left the old break showing, and gave both proverbs to the pot and the fire, never to a person. The dressed grain lay covered and unfigured, the charcoal unread beneath her finger, and the widow’s mark hung untouched, for a hearth and a morning and a bed are not openings.

Ilva drew at the yard well on the thirteenth with the rope stiff in the cold, clay pale in her nail crescents and rack dust in one thumb seam she did not scrub out. To a woman who asked what Stone’s firings had taken she answered, \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her hand to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and her mouth after both. On the fourteenth Hessa Rale came down the clay road from Greybank with Berr Clay’s slate edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned toward her own sleeve, the second strap let out; she read nothing aloud and did not look into the basket. Four rooms kept the same gap in their count, four likenesses and not one account — an account wanting a hand to lay them together and a payer under all four, and no such hand stood.

On the fifteenth evening, setting the boy on his bed and righting the fold where the cold had ridden it back, Sella tucked the wool into the empty place beside the crust. No word went with it, no third crust was put there, no name spoken over the place, no look toward his face; her hand rested the half-beat longer than the setting needed and went away. The boy took the interval apart by what was there and by what was not and filed it beside the crust’s gap, the shelf’s two gaps, the gone pan’s round ring and the field’s empty place — not a joining of rooms, not a third crust, not a gift, not a payment, no payer standing, gathered once and not made again. The crust kept its hair-lifted corner, and now the wool lay in the empty place without a name. Three days went by exact and told by nobody, and the count went on.
\end{CRchronicle}
